A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same MICo-150K, MICo-Bench, and Qwen-MICo research. Their main text, equations, three tables, twenty figures, and appendices support comparison. v2's internal reporting inconsistencies do not constitute missing material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training evaluations in Table 2, a three-image comparison in Table 3, and human-study, demographic, and metric-validation results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports revised model-evaluation results in Table 2 and retains original human-study, demographic, qualitative, and supplementary experimental results.

M1.justification: The Compose-by-Retrieval and De&Re data-construction pipelines, generative architectures, and model fine-tuning procedures remain unchanged. Qwen-Image-MICo denotes the existing Qwen-MICo baseline. Evaluation-metric changes are assessed under E3 and T1.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same source datasets, seven composition subtasks, 27 fine-grained types, De&Re task, and appendix application examples. The reduced benchmark sample counts do not establish changed task or population coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5.2 newly reports Gemini-3-Pro-Image-Preview and GPT-Image-1.5 comparisons, including an overall score and task rankings, and adds a benchmark-level Qwen-Image-2509 comparison. However, Table 2 retains its original comparator rows, and Table 3 retains the same two methods; the expanded comparisons are documented only in prose.

E3.justification: MICo-Bench changes from 1,000 cases, grouped as 200/200/300/300, to 897 cases grouped as 138/168/291/300. Sections 4.2 and 7.4 replace GPT-4o scoring with GPT-5.4, Qwen2.5-VL-72B verification with Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct, and binary facial-preservation thresholds with graded scores. These substantially revise the reported evaluation protocol without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The same De&Re ablation conditions remain in Table 2 despite removal of their explanatory prose. The appendix retains the human-alignment, style-homology, evaluator-coupling, copy-paste, demographic, and qualitative analyses. No new analytical question or robustness test is documented; revised numerical results are assessed under E6.

E5.justification: Both versions average human-ranking Spearman correlations across 25 participants and retain the same correlation-reporting procedures. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: Table 2 extensively replaces scores: Qwen-Image's real-De&Re overall score changes from 58.2 to 35.9, BAGEL's from 44.3 to 34.4, and OmniGen2's from 51.2 to 33.8, reversing BAGEL and OmniGen2's ordering. These are results under revised conditions, not comparable performance declines. Section 5.2 additionally reports Gemini's 51.76 and new leadership findings absent from Table 2. Table 3 and appendix validation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 7.4.1 substantively revises the visibility-weight definition: binary face acceptance above task-dependent thresholds becomes a five-level mapping to 0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.7, or 1, averaged with binary non-face scores. The geometric-mean SC/PQ definitions remain equivalent, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The principal dataset, benchmark, metric, and fine-tuning contributions remain. The benchmark claim changes from a balanced 1,000-case collection to 897 cases. The introduction and conclusion shift the Qwen-Image-2509 comparison from three-image performance to benchmark-level superiority, although the abstract retains its earlier three-image matching claim.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 removes the explicit conclusion that curated synthetic targets can substitute for real targets. Section 7.4.1 removes the interpretation linking very high facial similarity to copy-paste artifacts and its threshold rationale. Existing demographic limitations and appendix interpretations of style bias and evaluator coupling remain.

D1.justification: Section 7.1 changes a promised release upon acceptance to reported availability of the dataset, benchmark annotations and images, and complete evaluation scripts and prompts. v2 also documents face-source indices and a replaceable VLM interface. Conversely, it removes Table 2's ablation-column definitions and the per-type sampling allocations for the 75-case human study and 108-case style analysis.

R1.justification: v2 removes WithAnyone, cited as reference 90 in v1 to support the facial-similarity discussion. The remaining related-work discussion and research positioning are largely unchanged; subsequent reference renumbering is not a substantive change.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the evaluator, benchmark, results, release, and metric-detail passages. v2 also adds Kai Cui and revises affiliations, corrects terminology and typos, and removes several explanatory paragraphs. The overall section structure and most main-text and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: All twenty figures and three tables are retained, with unchanged embedded example images and plots. Figure 6 moves between columns, appendix spacing changes, and several captions are revised. Table 2's new caption removes the ablation legend and describes different bolding semantics despite retaining the existing column structure.

improvement.justification: v2 improves release documentation and specifies its revised evaluator, but weakens the connection between claims and evidence. Unlike v1's corresponding discussion, Section 5.2 attributes leadership results to models absent from Table 2, while Table 2 loses explanations of its retained ablation columns. The changed evaluator is also not explicitly reconciled with unchanged appendix validation results. These reporting regressions make the revised empirical claims harder to audit, outweighing the documentation gains.
